transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-22
Time: 17:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Sara Patel (Blueleaf Head of Search), Jonah Kim (Eng Manager), Priya Singh (Security)

Summary: quick walkthrough of hosted embeddings + rerank endpoints, demo of search relevance flow, Q&A on security and perf, agree pilot next steps

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I know we have an hour, we'll keep it tight. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, with Diego our systems SE.
[00:08] Sara: Hi, Sara here - excited to see how this could improve our search relevance.
[00:12] Jonah: Jonah here, curious about latency impact; we have a 200ms SLA tail for our web search.
[00:18] Priya: Priya - I'll be listening for security and data residency bits.
[00:22] Maya: Great. Quick agenda: show the hosted embeddings and the rerank endpoint, talk about tradeoffs (latency vs cost), then security and pilot details.
[00:31] Diego: I'll demo a sample pipeline - retrieve with embeddings in the vector DB, then call Redwood's rerank endpoint to rescore top-k. We'll show response times on hosted API. Please note transcription may mangle some terms.
[01:00] (demo starts)
[01:12] Diego: So first, embeddings. We take query -> call /v1/embeddings, get a 1024-d vector (here we're using our 1024x model but dims vary by model). Blueleaf you mentioned you use 512 dims today?
[01:26] Sara: Yeah mostly 512, some older models are 300. We're open to 1024 if perf is worth it.
[01:33] Diego: Ok. Higher dims often help recall but increase index storage and ANN search cost. For hosted we recommend starting with 512/768 for parity and then try 1024 if you need finer granularity.
[01:48] Jonah: For production, we use Annoy and Faiss in-house - will Redwood embeddings be compatible with our index?
[01:55] Diego: Yes - the embeddings are standard float arrays. You can index them in Faiss/Annoy or use Redwood's integrated vector store if you want managed ops. A common pattern: create index in your infra, run k-NN to get top 100, then call rerank.
[02:12] Sara: About rerank - what's the API pattern?
[02:15] Diego: Two options. Option A: retrieve candidates with your vector DB, then call Redwood's rerank endpoint with the query + candidate docs; Redwood runs a cross-attention re-ranker (cost higher per request but much better precision). Option B: do a single-stage retrieval-only approach which is cheaper but less precise. For web UX we often recommend retrieve-then-rerank for the top 10-50 candidates.
[02:43] Sara: How does latency look for rerank? Our target 200ms tail is tough.
[02:47] Diego: On hosted API with a small model optimized for rerank, median for a 10-item rerank is ~80-120ms; tail depends on request batching and model. For strict 200ms tail you'll want the dedicated pool or a smaller model variant and prefix caching. Also we support streaming for token heavy outputs but rerank responses are small so streaming isn't relevant.
[03:12] Jonah: What's the per-request cost ballpark?
[03:15] Maya: We'll send exact pricing, but rough: retrieval (embeddings) cost per query + rerank call cost which is based on token compute and model. For many customers the rerank is the bigger contributor; Optimize can suggest batching/caching to reduce unit cost.
[03:34] (screen share: demo app)
[03:41] Diego: Here's a live demo - I run a query, we call embeddings, Faiss returns 50 candidates, then rerank endpoint returns reordered list. Note the response times in the console: embeddings 18ms, ANN 24ms, rerank 96ms, total ~140ms.
[03:58] Sara: Nice. A few questions - can we do partial rerank, like rerank only the top 5?
[04:03] Diego: Absolutely - common to rerank top 5 or 10 to reduce cost. Redwood's rerank lets you set candidate size.
[04:12] Priya: On data handling - when we send doc text for rerank, is that persisted? What about logs and PII?
[04:20] Maya: Great question. For hosted, by default request logs are retained for short debugging windows; we can disable retention for your account. We also have VPC/private deployment options and Dedicated pools if you need strict isolation. We support KMS integrations for encryption at rest and in transit, and audit logs for all API calls.
[04:40] Priya: Do you have SOC 2 and penetration test reports?
[04:43] Maya: Yes - we'll share the SOC 2 report and the network diagram. Also our security page has details on pen tests.
[04:50] Priya: And SSO and RBAC?
[04:52] Maya: SSO (SAML/OIDC) and RBAC are supported for Private/Dedicated customers; hosted accounts also have team roles and API key scopes.
[05:05] Jonah: Back to performance - you mentioned caching. How does Redwood handle prefix/KV cache - is that automatic?
[05:12] Diego: We do automatic KV caching for decoder-heavy workloads and prefix caching for repeated prompts. For rerank it's less applicable but there are caching opportunities for embeddings and for commonly seen candidate sets; Optimize can recommend cache TTLs.
[05:28] Sara: For us the tricky part is scale - we serve 5k qps at peak. How would hosted handle that?
[05:34] Maya: For very high QPS we typically recommend Dedicated capacity with reserved GPU pools. Hosted can handle moderate scale but if you need predictable throughput at 5k qps you'd look at Dedicated or hybrid routing.
[05:47] Diego: Also smart routing can fallback to smaller models when capacity constrained; that's how we do graceful degradation.
[05:56] (demo: show API call examples)
[06:05] Diego: Example curl for embeddings: 
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-768","input":"..."}'
Response: vector of floats. Then do your ANN search, take top_k. Then call rerank: 
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -d '{"model":"redwood-rerank-small","query":"...","candidates":[{"id":"...","text":"..."}, ...]}'

[06:35] (minor transcription glitch: 'redwood' transcribed as 'redwooded' briefly)
[06:40] Sara: Do you have a hosted vector store or do we keep our own?
[06:44] Diego: We offer both - managed vector store as an add-on, or you can host the index in your infra. Many customers prefer the managed option for ops simplicity; others keep the index close to their data for latency and control.
[06:58] Jonah: For the pilot we'd like to run with our index and just call rerank on Redwood. Is that straightforward?
[07:03] Maya: Yes, that's a very common pilot - we ask for a sample dataset, Diego will run a benchmark and we'll instrument the calls.
[07:12] Priya: Any requirements for PII redaction?
[07:15] Diego: We recommend you do client-side redaction for any sensitive fields before sending; Redwood also provides tools and policies for request filtering.
[07:24] (15 min demo interlude showing variations: top-5 vs top-20, model selection)
[22:10] Diego: Showing an A/B: attention to model choice - small rerank model gives 70-80% of quality at 40% cost. Larger cross-attention model increases relevance but spikes cost.
[22:28] Sara: If we wanted to optimize costs, what are levers?
[22:31] Diego: Short list: reduce candidate size (top_k), use a smaller rerank model for most queries and larger for high-value queries, enable batching for low-latency tolerant endpoints, use caching for repeated queries, quantization for dedicated pools. Our Optimize product automates many suggestions and estimates cost impact.
[22:50] Jonah: For batching - does hosted batch across customers? That concerns us for data isolation.
[22:57] Maya: Hosted batching is per-tenant; we do not cross-tenant batch mixing for customer data. For Dedicated there's even stronger isolation.
[23:08] Priya: Encryption at rest - keys?
[23:11] Maya: KMS integrations supported (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer-managed keys for private). We'll include KMS notes in the docs we share.
[23:20] (transcript shows some filler: umm, ahh)
[23:32] Diego: Performance metric we track: p50/p95/p99 for rerank and embeddings separately. We'll provide sample dashboards from Redwood Console so you can see token-level cost breakdown.
[23:50] Sara: Ok great - about evaluation - if we roll out to prod how do we monitor quality regressions?
[23:56] Maya: Redwood supports eval/test sets and regression alerts tied to prompt sets; you can run periodic evals comparing current model vs new model and alert on NDCG or precision drops.
[24:12] Jonah: Does Redwood offer A/B rollout for live traffic?
[24:15] Diego: Yes - Canary/A-B rollouts with automatic fallback policies. You can route a percentage of traffic to new model and monitor metrics.
[24:25] Priya: Audit logs retention?
[24:28] Maya: Configurable; for enterprise accounts we can meet longer retention requirements and export logs to your S3 or SIEM.
[24:37] (short silence / note taking)
[24:52] Sara: Real world question - we've seen hallucinations in rerank when docs are noisy. Does rerank exacerbate or reduce hallucination?
[24:59] Diego: Rerank reduces hallucination relative to generation-first approaches because it ranks candidate docs - it doesn't synthesize new facts. However if you send noisy docs the model might still surface wrong context; we recommend candidate filtering and conservative reranker prompts.
[25:20] Maya: We also support tool calling and structured outputs for other use-cases but not usually for pure rerank.
[25:30] (demo ends)
[25:35] Maya: Quick recap and pilot proposal: 2-week pilot, run 2k queries, measure p50/p95 latencies and NDCG uplift vs baseline. Diego will run benchmarks with your sample; Sara/Jonah will provide dataset and acceptance criteria.
[25:50] Sara: Sounds good. We'll provide a dataset and define success metrics - target p95 < 200ms and NDCG +0.08 over baseline.
[25:59] Jonah: Also want a clear TCO comparison for Hosted vs Dedicated for steady 5k qps.
[26:05] Maya: We'll model both and send back an excel-style TCO.
[26:10] Priya: Please include details on SOC2, encryption, and SSO in that packet.
[26:14] Maya: Will do.
[26:20] Diego: I'll note a couple technical follow-ups: need sample docs, a few representative queries, and your current index config. Also we'll capture profile of sequence lengths.
[26:32] Action items recapped.
[26:36] (transcription oddity: 'KV cache' appears as 'K V cash' once)
[26:45] Maya: Any other questions?
[26:48] Jonah: One last - can we run a dedicated benchmark with our Faiss settings?
[26:53] Diego: Yes, we can replicate Faiss config locally for benchmarking. It helps to include your index params.
[26:59] Sara: Ok we'll share.
[27:05] Maya: Thanks everyone - we'll send the materials and proposed pilot timeline today.
[27:12] Priya: Thanks, that's helpful.
[27:15] (meeting ends; note the rest of time was used for internal Redwood post-call)

End of transcript.

Recap (as spoken):
- Demo of embeddings + rerank flow, showed ~140ms end-to-end in-hosted example.
- Discussed retrieval strategies, candidate size, model selection and caching.
- Security: SOC2, KMS, SSO, audit logs covered - Redwood to share docs.
- Agreed pilot: 2-week benchmark, Diego to run tests, Maya to send pricing + docs.
